title: Social Eye Gaze in Human-Robot Interaction: A Review
method_context: Narrative review separating human-, design- and technology-focused gaze investigations.

findings.claim: Implementing gaze and measuring its human effects are distinct research goals.
Face-directed behavior without reciprocity is not mutual gaze; joint attention concerns a shared referent.

limitations: A broad historical review does not validate a particular small display or implementation.
notes: Full-text passages and publication details inspected online on 13 October 2026. Also used as the pre-2019 domain-specific style exemplar.

title: Eyes ahead: a scoping review of technologies enabling humanoid robots to follow human gaze
method_context: Scoping review of humanoid systems estimating human gaze and mapping it to environmental targets.

findings.claim: Gaze following requires gaze estimation and environmental mapping rather than face-position tracking alone.
Most reviewed studies omit response-time information such as detection-to-reaction latency.

limitations: Its gaze-following scope is adjacent to face-following companions, not identical.
Abstract and discussion report inconsistent study totals; the manuscript does not reproduce either total.
notes: Publisher full text and citation checked 13 October 2026. Published 16 January 2026; volume 12 is labeled 2025.

title: Low-cost social robot designs for education: a review
method_context: Review of 34 affordable educational robot designs.

findings.claim: Designs use varied display and computing arrangements, including combined microcontroller and higher-level computing architectures.
Affordability depends on application resources and continuing infrastructure costs.

limitations: Educational robot designs do not supply a universal cost threshold for miniature companions.
Grey literature is outside the review search.
notes: Publisher methods, discussion and bibliographic identity checked 13 October 2026.

title: How Do We Research Human-Robot Interaction in the Age of Large Language Models? A Systematic Review
method_context: Author-preprint abstract of a systematic review reporting 86 included articles.

findings.claim: LLM-HRI studies use varied experimental setups, methods and evaluation measures.

limitations: Only abstract-level claims are used; no individual-study or methods detail is inferred.
notes: ArXiv metadata and abstract checked 13 October 2026. Associated CHI publication DOI 10.1145/3772318.3790920 is linked by arXiv; author version is cited explicitly.

title: SANRA—a scale for the quality assessment of narrative review articles
method_context: Editorial appraisal scale developed and tested on medical narrative-review manuscripts.

findings.claim: The six items address importance, aims, search description, references, reasoning and endpoint information.

limitations: Medical-domain development does not establish validation as a robotics review standard.
notes: Original article inspected online 13 October 2026; used as an editorial checklist, with no numerical score assigned.

title: A visual perceptual perspective on gaze in social robotics
method_context: Theoretical perspective on perceptual and communicative gaze functions.

findings.claim: Looking direction should not be equated with visual attention, and perceptual and individual differences matter.
The article focuses on humanoid and anthropomorphic robots and limits generalization to other forms.

limitations: Not a new observer experiment validating stylized screen eyes.
notes: Publisher text and citation verified 13 October 2026; volume 33, article 131.

title: Taming Mona Lisa: Communicating Gaze Faithfully in 2D and 3D Facial Projections
method_context: Within-subject flat-versus-3D projection comparison with five observers at five positions, 1.8 m from the face.

findings.claim: The three-dimensional projection supported viewpoint-independent interpretation of gaze in physical space relative to the tested flat projection.

limitations: Five observers and a particular projection geometry.
An omitted stimulus-angle range due to a programming error is acknowledged in Section 3.2.
notes: Existing full PDF and extraction inspected 13 October 2026; title page gives January 2012, volume 1, issue 2, article 11.

title: Breaking the Mona Lisa Effect: Enhancing Eye Contact with Virtual Humans in 2D Display Environments
method_context: Within-subject gaze judgments by 30 university participants; 65-inch display, 2.4 m distance; 5-degree and 15-degree arrangements.

findings.claim: Small virtual-camera rotation improved left/right gaze recognition in the narrow 5-degree arrangement.

limitations: Only a constrained two-observer arrangement.
Gaze judgment without conversation; dialogue transfer remains future work.
The 15-degree condition always preceded the 5-degree condition.
notes: Full supplied/cached proceedings PDF read 13 October 2026. CEUR Workshop Proceedings 3467, APMAR 2023; no DOI invented.

title: Mirror Eyes: Explainable Human-Robot Interaction at a Glance
method_context: Within-subject robot pick-and-place task with 33 participants, screen eyes, an actuated head, speech and programmed errors.

findings.claim: Mirrored target imagery increased subjective information-processing awareness and enabled earlier interruption of erroneous actions.
findings.locator: Sections II-D, III-A and III-B; Table II

limitations: Very brief exposure, primarily engineering/science participants.
No miniature-display legibility or cost evaluation.
notes: ArXiv v1 HTML and identity inspected 13 October 2026. Associated RO-MAN publication DOI 10.1109/RO-MAN63969.2025.11217810 is linked by arXiv; inspected author version is labeled.

title: Conversational Gaze Aversion for Humanlike Robots
method_context: Thirty-participant NAO study comparing well-timed, poorly timed and absent aversion, across conversation tasks.

findings.claim: Well-timed aversion improved thoughtfulness judgments and conversational floor management.
findings.locator: Section 5 Results and Discussion, PDF pp. 6-7

findings.claim: Well-timed aversion did not increase self-disclosure measured by response word count.

limitations: Head-mediated gaze differs from pixel-only pupils.
Scripted task-specific timing is not a general engagement result.
notes: Original cached paper methods/results/limitations and metadata inspected 13 October 2026.

title: Modeling Feedback in Interaction With Conversational Agents—A Review
method_context: Review of agent-to-user and user-to-agent feedback across speech, facial cues, gaze and head gestures.

findings.claim: Feedback distinguishes contact, perception, understanding and attitude/acceptance.

limitations: Feedback categories do not establish that a particular animation is understood by users.
notes: Publisher text, Table 1 and identity checked 13 October 2026.

title: How Quickly Should a Communication Robot Respond? Delaying Strategies and Habituation Effects
method_context: Publisher abstract describes robot response-time preference, filler strategy and habituation investigations.

findings.claim: Response-time preferences peaked at one second in the first experiment; conversational fillers notified listeners of intent to respond.

limitations: Full-text methods and sample unavailable in this task; no sample or effect size claimed.
Speech response timing does not establish a universal gaze-motion threshold.
notes: Publisher abstract and metadata verified 13 October 2026.

title: Fluid-Xpress: Emotion-Aware Dual-Loop Framework for Empathic Facial Reaction in HRI
method_context: Separate nonverbal and verbal processing loops; within-subject pilot with eight female university students and counterbalanced conditions.

findings.claim: The architecture separates nonverbal facial reactions from verbal reasoning.
Expression-awareness ratings improved, while between-condition valence change did not differ significantly.
findings.locator: Sections 4 and 5, Table 1 and Figure 3; journal pp. 427-428

limitations: Small, homogeneous pilot and brief sessions.
The isolated 0.05-ms anecdotal latency in the source is not a defined camera-to-pixel benchmark and is omitted.
notes: Original cached published PDF inspected 13 October 2026; cited page range 425-429 excludes repository front matter.

title: Age of Information: An Introduction and Survey
method_context: Survey of timestamped status updates and information-age models.

findings.claim: Age of Information measures elapsed time since generation of the freshest delivered update and differs from delay and throughput.
Sampling and queueing policy affect age; minimum delay does not guarantee minimum age.

limitations: Networking analysis is not a validated measure of social presence.
Its transfer to renderer-target age is proposed interpretation.
notes: Original cached author-hosted published PDF definition and queueing sections inspected 13 October 2026.

title: Update or Wait: How to Keep Your Data Fresh
method_context: Generate-at-will status-update model with channel feedback and random service times; theoretical optimization.

findings.claim: Immediately generating the next update after delivery does not always minimize average information age.
findings.locator: Abstract, Section I and Section V

limitations: Assumptions of its channel model are not established for Iris's camera, speech workload and TCP path.
notes: ArXiv v9 full text inspected; published metadata independently verified against the Rutgers institutional record on 13 October 2026. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 63(11), 7492-7508.

title: FluxGarage RoboEyes
method_context: Maintainer README of an Arduino library for animated OLED eyes.

findings.claim: The repository documents animated eye rendering on OLED displays.

limitations: Software repository, not peer-reviewed social-effectiveness evidence.
notes: Inspected 13 October 2026; year represents access year, not a claimed release year. Repository is excluded from the scholarly-study count.

title: XiaoZhi ESP32
method_context: Maintainer README of an ESP32 conversational-device project.

findings.claim: The repository documents conversational audio pipelines and display-capable embedded devices.
findings.locator: README Features Implemented and supported hardware

limitations: Software repository; its feature list is not an empirical human-interaction outcome.
notes: Inspected 13 October 2026; access year only. Excluded from the scholarly-study count.
